![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/dcf7a2ea5b44f3f5ba7b1663f7979cdc3fc8c1036b6cc797904ffda77f1003bd.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the сurve is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is true while statement II is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$  assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/818ad935fd7aa592f00c23c9c77799d127449b4bb6ffacee4354e7acf39887d8.png)

So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- Statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/70e268a08195a92573f41927ae7de653837fca273f0c75cb951243a31ec660a2.png)

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
